To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Occupants are willing to participate in HVAC control if they are provided a feedback loop, (2) Occupants can provide useful feedback about the HVAC system, and (3) Occupants can be effectively engaged to provide feedback about HVAC settings.
the ZonePAC architecture is effective at providing a means for building occupants to participate in zonal HVAC control settings that directly affect building scale energy consumption.

(1) the ZonePAC framework is effective in reducing the building energy consumption by 15%, (2) the framework is effective in improving occupant satisfaction by 10%, and (3) the framework has the potential to reduce building energy consumption by up to 30% and occupant dissatisfaction by 20% if the HVAC control system can be made to respond to the feedback provided by the ZonePAC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a distributed control architecture that can be used to effectively manage energy in commercial buildings.
the design and deployment of an embedded sensor system that enables the occupants to provide zonal information to the HVAC control system.
the design of a distributed sensing and control infrastructure for building HVAC systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ZonePAC is an effective, scalable and robust system to enable zonal HVAC control.
ZonePAC is a viable and effective system that provides a new way of thinking about the design of building control systems that can provide a new level of comfort and energy efficiency.
ZonePAC provides a viable, effective and scalable approach for zonal HVAC control and energy management in commercial buildings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ZonePAC is a viable and effective solution that enables the occupants to participate in the HVAC control of their immediate surroundings.

ZonePAC provides for the following: a) a low-cost, low-maintenance and low-energy embedded sensing infrastructure that is scalable to thousands of zones in a large building b) an information management infrastructure for the collection, storage, analysis and dissemination of the data collected by the sensors c) a control architecture that provides for the participation of building occupants in the control loop of the building HVAC system d) a user interface that provides for the effective interaction with occupants in the control of their zones.
ZonePAC is a viable solution to the challenges of building HVAC control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
occupants are willing and able to participate in building scale control systems if they are given the right tools.
the building scale HVAC system can be effectively controlled by a distributed sensing and control architecture that involves building occupants in zoned control settings.
the building occupants can be a valuable partner in the energy conservation effort.
